trickyParts: Naming `owns` in reconcileNow tightened four guards that had only the fence, by adding the host comparison. Each protects a write the next pass redoes - `inboundOpenFor`, `establishedSession` and `ensureHeartbeat`, all of which the pass a move queues clears or repeats - so the tightening only stops a pass that was already doomed. The handoff's predecessor round listed them one by one.

`observeAbandonedHold` answers `true` when fenced, the answer that records no refusal: a refusal written in error outlives every later pass through `refusedRoles`, while a refusal left unwritten costs one more claim. That asymmetry is why the fenced answer is not `false`.

The blocker's test guards the pair of re-reads rather than each one, because either alone prevents the write. That is right for an invariant test and wrong to leave implicit, so it is on the thread, in the body and here.

GitHub ran no workflow at all for the pre-merge head eb379142: while a pull request conflicts with its base, no `on: pull_request` workflow runs for any of its activity types. The absence of runs was the signal that the branch had gone CONFLICTING, not a slow queue.
deviations: The architect asked for the convention to be made to hold for the next person, preferring a test, then a type, then a lint rule. I took the test, which is the reviewer's own first preference and the shape it named. I did not build the type-level write gate: the two invariant tests assert the outcomes the four findings would have produced, and a gate over the six shared names is a refactor of about 28 write sites that this round, already the fourth, is the wrong place for. The residual - that neither test fails if one guard of a redundant pair is removed, and that nothing stops the next await from missing the predicate - is written into the body's Not proven / risk entry rather than left implicit.

The forward merge's fingerprint CHANGED, e9e6a5e0 -> d5eac4b3, and the whole of the change is two lines: before the merge this branch added the `### Added` heading in packages/envoy-client/CHANGELOG.md itself; after it, main supplies that heading and the branch adds only its entry under it. The two diffs carry the same file set and are otherwise identical, which is quoted in the rebase comment on the pull request.
discoveredComplexity: A conflicting pull request is silent in CI: no run is queued, so a head can look untested when it is actually unrunnable. `gh pr view --json mergeable` is what distinguishes the two, and it is worth reading whenever a push produces no runs.

The margin check has grown from three rules to five across three rounds, each time because a hand-copied constant was found unguarded by a reviewer rather than by the build. The remaining copies named in its header are the ones nobody has yet shown to drift.
